thread:
alex: quick heads-up — I finished initial onboarding for NeedlePoint-v2 embeddings on the semantic-sim benchmark. ran quantized and fp16 baselines. short summary below, throwing it in here for triage.

alex: TL;DR: recall@1 down ~2.8% vs fp16 on short queries, recall@10 flat. int8-per-channel very close to fp16 for >=128-dims.

meenal: nice. can you paste the exact eval config? which dataset split?

alex: sure — used semeval-small holdout (8k queries), batchsize=512, max_len=128, dim=768.

alex: eval command I ran:
```bash
python eval_embeddings.py --model needlepoint-v2 --quant int8_pc --batch 512 --dataset semeval_small --metric recall_at_k
```

sasha: do you have the numbers? even quick ones help.

alex: yup. raw outputs:
```
Model                recall@1   recall@5   recall@10
needlepoint-v2-fp16   0.742      0.882      0.915
needlepoint-v2-int8   0.713      0.881      0.916
needlepoint-v2-int8pc 0.737      0.880      0.914
```

alex: note: int8 (naive per-tensor) dropped a bit on @1. per-channel quant (int8pc) recovered most of that.

oliver: interesting that recall@10 is basically unchanged. suggests nearest-neighbor ordering mostly preserved for the top-10 margin.

meenal: can we sanity-check with clustering metric? silhouette or cohesion?

alex: ran quick silhouette (cosine) on 5k sample: fp16=0.18, int8=0.14, int8pc=0.17. so same pattern.

sasha: any sign of catastrophic embedding collapse on few classes? e.g., some centroids overlapping?

alex: spotted a tiny cluster shift for queries with very short text (<6 tokens) — avg L2 shift ~0.08 between fp16 and int8pc. attaching short snippet:
```
# sample short-query shift pairs
q1: "reset password"    fp16->int8pc cos=0.987
q2: "pricing"           fp16->int8pc cos=0.942
q3: "refund"            fp16->int8pc cos=0.823  <-- this one notable
```

alex: the refund case moved enough to drop from rank1 to rank3 in int8pc. looks like low-context queries are fragile.

meenal: ok. what's the next step — more targeted short-query holdouts or tweak quant params?

oliver: also worth checking sequence length behavior — are short queries being padded differently during encoding with quant kernels? kernels sometimes change numeric stability for short seqs.

alex: good point. I re-ran with explicit attention_mask handling (no extra padding) and the delta shrank by ~0.6% on recall@1. so padding mismatch likely part of it.

sasha: do we have a candidate fallback policy? e.g., route short queries to fp16 (hosted) and others to int8pc? cost tradeoff?

meenal: rough cost math: fp16 per-token cost ~3.2x int8pc. but short queries have few tokens so routing short ones to fp16 might be cost-neutral while improving quality. need telemetry sim.

alex: added a quick sim: with current traffic distribution (short queries ~12% of traffic), expected overall cost increase ~8% but recall@1 recovers ~1.6% absolute.

oliver: that's reasonable if svc SLOs allow it. open question: is routing complexity worth it vs improving quant config?

alex: next experiments I propose: 1) sweep per-channel quant bitwidth (8 -> 6) for short queries, 2) run targeted short-query holdout with larger batch variance, 3) collect more human evals for the top-5 differences.

sasha: pls add a short checklist in the ticket and I'll pick up the human eval part. also tag support for rollout rule if we decide routing fallback.

alex: added checklist to the onboarding ticket: https://rwd.atlassian.com/browse/ML-ONB-912 (notes + raw csv).

ci-bot: Build passed on needlepoint-v2-int8pc pipeline :white_check_mark:

meenal: awesome. thanks alex. leave the ticket in triage, will sync tomorrow in the embed standup. :thumbsup:
